title: Change an NES game: press the caught Game Pak to pop it up, swap in the spare, press it down to catch, shut the lid
instruction: Swap the game in the console for the spare one: put the old game on the empty stand, load the spare and leave the console closed, ready to play.
context: On the original NES-001 front-loader a loaded Game Pak is held down by a hidden push-push catch: it must be pressed down until it pops up before it can be pulled, slid in fully, then pressed down until it catches. Nintendo's manual: 'Gently push down on the Game Pak allowing it to pop up. Do not attempt to pry the Game Pak up. Pull the Game Pak out.' A pulled, prised or popped-up Game Pak means no game; changing games is an everyday home job.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. Console: Nintendo Entertainment System NES-001, 25.6 wide x 20.3 deep x 8.9 cm tall (fixed; about 2.3 kg on rubber feet), grey, front face centred at (34.5, 0) facing the robot, standing on a 3 cm pine shelf board 25.2 deep x 32 cm wide set flush with its recessed black front strip. Chamber lid: the console's top-front panel, 6.8 cm deep and 14.1 cm wide, hinged at its back edge 8.75 cm up, with a 4.35 cm front face whose lower edge stands out 8 mm as a finger ledge; it starts shut and opens to 110 degrees, where it rests past its balance point (about 103 degrees). Inside: the cartridge carrier (black rails with 1.5 mm side play on the Game Pak, and the 72-pin connector, its stop face 13.95 cm behind the console's front face) pivots at the connector; pressed past its catch it pops up 0.10 rad (label end about 14 mm higher). Old game: an NES Game Pak, 12.0 x 13.3 x 2.0 cm, grey with a red label, loaded label up, connector end in, label end 6 mm behind the front face, carrier caught down. Spare game: the same with a blue label, lying flat label up on the robot's left stand with its label end toward the robot, overhanging the stand's front by 5 cm. Stands: two pine display blocks 8 deep x 10 wide x 6 cm tall, centred at (29.5, 15.0) and (29.5, -15.0). Lot B moves the spare to the right stand (same pose). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Both arms start at their ready pose with the grippers open.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: any point of the loaded game moves more than 5 mm before its catch has been released (pulled or prised while caught); either game tips more than 15 degrees out of the carrier's plane while any part of it is inside the chamber (prised); or the spare slides home onto the connector while the carrier is down, caught or held down (label end more than 7 mm below popped-up; the carrier must be up to take a Game Pak). Otherwise the final state counts, only with both hands at least 5 mm from both games, the lid and the carrier and everything still for the last 1 s: 0 unless the old game lies flat (within 10 degrees) on a stand with its middle over the stand's top; 0.25 if it does but the spare is not fully in; 0.5 if the spare is also fully in (connector end within 3 mm of fully home, square within 5 degrees, label up) but the carrier is not caught down; 0.75 if the carrier is also caught down (label end at its down position within 1.1 mm and staying there with the hands clear) but the lid is open; 1.0 if the lid is also shut (front edge within 3 mm). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz), about 1.5 times the 103.1 s demo
reset_notes: 1. Set the console on its shelf board at its mark, front to the robot. 2. Load the red-label Game Pak label up, push it in to the connector and press it down until it catches; shut the lid. 3. Lay the blue-label Game Pak flat, label up, on the lot's stand (A: robot's left; B: robot's right), label end toward the robot and 5 cm over the stand's front edge. 4. Leave the other stand empty. 5. Return both arms to the ready pose with the grippers open.
fidelity: Rigid boxes at the NES-001's published 25.6 x 20.3 x 8.9 cm outline and the Game Pak's 12.0 x 13.3 x 2.0 cm. Chamber, lid, carrier travel (0.10 rad), spring (about 5.5 N at the label end), masses and frictions are estimates. The push-push catch is code: a joint stop that toggles each time the carrier is pressed 2.6 mm below down. The 72-pin connector is a stop face; its light grip on the board edge and electrical contact are not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, both at the step limit); demo: 1.0 in each lot
